hero.headline: Garage Door Spring Repair in Chicago, IL
hero.subheadline: That bang you heard from the garage was probably a torsion spring letting go. We replace both springs with high-cycle steel and have your door balanced the same day — anywhere from Albany Park to Mount Greenwood.

intro: A snapped spring is the single most common garage door failure in Chicago, and it never picks a convenient morning. The door suddenly weighs its full 150–300 pounds, the opener strains and gives up, and your car is stuck behind a slab of steel. Our technicians replace torsion and extension springs across every Chicago neighborhood — the bungalow belts of Portage Park and Jefferson Park, Beverly's brick garages, Bridgeport two-flats, and new-construction infill from Albany Park to the South Loop. We quote the complete flat price before touching a wrench, replace springs in matched pairs so the fresh one isn't fighting a tired one, and finish with a full balance and safety test. Book online any hour and the 10% discount applies automatically.
localContext: Chicago's housing stock is hard on springs in a specific way: most of the city's garages are detached, unheated frame structures on rear alleys, built decades before anyone imagined a 16-foot insulated door. Inside an unheated alley garage, January cold makes spring steel brittle exactly when lake-effect snow adds friction load to every lift — which is why the week after each cold snap is our busiest spring-replacement stretch of the year. Add road-salt spray drifting in under the door and you get corrosion pitting that shortens spring life well below the rated cycle count.

problemSigns.sign: A loud bang from the garage
problemSigns.detail: The classic Chicago alley-garage sound in January — a torsion spring unwinding all its stored energy at once. The door is now unsafe to lift by hand.

problemSigns.sign: Door lifts a few inches, then stops
problemSigns.detail: The opener's force limit is giving up against the door's full dead weight. Forcing it strips the opener's drive gear — now it's two repairs.

problemSigns.sign: Visible gap in the spring above the door
problemSigns.detail: A healthy torsion spring is one continuous coil. A two-inch gap means it has already failed, even if the door still moves.
On older extension-spring doors common in pre-war Chicago garages, one spring often fails quietly first — the door works, badly, until the second one goes.
When a spring lets go, the lift cables lose tension and can jump their drums. Don't operate the door — the cables may be the only thing holding it square.

faqs.q: How fast can you replace a spring in Chicago?
faqs.a: Usually same-day. Our trucks work the city in zones, so a morning call from Portage Park or Beverly typically gets an afternoon slot at the latest — and emergency calls run 24 hours a day, Monday through Saturday.

faqs.q: Why do garage door springs snap so often in Chicago winters?
faqs.a: Most Chicago garages are unheated, detached alley structures. Sub-zero cold makes spring steel brittle while snow and ice add load to every lift, and road-salt corrosion pits the coils. That combination is why spring failures spike after every cold snap.

faqs.q: Do you replace both springs or just the broken one?
faqs.a: Both, always, on a two-spring door. The springs have identical mileage — pairing a new spring with a worn one unbalances the door and typically brings us back within months for the second failure.

faqs.q: Can I still open my door with a broken spring to get my car out?
faqs.a: Don't try. A Chicago-standard steel door weighs 150–300 pounds without spring assistance, and lifting it by hand or with the opener risks injury and a stripped opener gear. Call us instead — emergency dispatch can usually free a trapped car within hours.

faqs.q: What does spring replacement cost in Chicago?
faqs.a: Most torsion spring replacements land between $180 and $450 including parts, quoted flat before work starts. Booking online saves another 10%.
